images.title: Two copies make a parallelogram
images.purpose: Picture the trapezium joiner's core move: a trapezium and its turned copy snap into a parallelogram of base a + b.
images.composition: One parallelogram made of two trapeziums in two colours, the joint along a slanting side.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, the main figure large and centred with generous empty margins on all sides, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills, nothing else in the frame. Trapezium 1, filled #0072B2: bottom side 11 units, top side 7 units, height 6 units, corners at (0,0), (11,0), (9,6), (2,6). Trapezium 2, an identical copy turned half way round, filled #E69F00: corners at (11,0), (18,0), (20,6), (9,6), sharing the slanting side from (11,0) to (9,6) with trapezium 1. Together they form a parallelogram with corners (0,0), (18,0), (20,6), (2,6). A dashed #6B7280 height from (2,6) down to (2,0) with a right angle mark. Labels: 'b = 11' just under the bottom segment from (0,0) to (11,0), 'a = 7' just under the copy's bottom segment from (11,0) to (18,0), 'h = 6' beside the dashed height, a brace below both under the whole bottom edge labelled 'a + b = 18', and below the figure 'Trapezium = 1/2 × 18 × 6 = 54'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered

images.takeaway: Two copies make a parallelogram 18 by 6, so one trapezium is half of 108, which is 54.

image_decisions.why: A practice concept gets the tool's core manipulation in its simplest state: two copies joined into a parallelogram.
